phrases.syllabary_text: ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ ᏥᎷᎩ ᏌᎾᎴ ᎦᏳᎳᏅ ᏌᏊ ᎢᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᏱᏣᎶᏌ ᏙᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: kali'elik tsi'luhk snale ka'ylahn sakwu iywakat yitsalohs thv

phrases.english_text: I’m thankful for you coming here this morning. Already one time you have been through this, haven’t you?

phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Yes.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏏᏭᏛ ᏴᎬᏯᏅᏓᏗᏍᏓ ᏄᏰᎵᏛ ᏥᏂᏓᏛᏁᎭ

phrases.phonetic_broad: siwtv ykyanvtatist nuyelitv tsinittvnea
phrases.english_text: Again, I’ll remind you the purpose of what we’re doing.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: vhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Aha.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎯᎢᎾ ᏥᏓᎾᏕᎶᏆᎠ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎯᎠ ᏗᏜ ᏃᏭ ᏧᎾᏔᎾ ᏍᎩᏅ Ꮲ ᏱᏛᎾᎴᏅᎯ ᎠᎾᏛᏓᏍᏗᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: hi'ina tsitanatelhohkwa'a tnyol hi'a titla now tsunthan skinv tlhv yitvnlenhi anthvtahstihv ohst tsalk kawonihihst kehsv

phrases.english_text: Those that are learning, the children this way, the adults that way, someday they’ll start listening to it, good Cherokee speaking.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏐᎢᎴ ᎨᏒ Ꮭ ᏳᏓᎷᎳ ᏗᎨᏣᎵᏏ ᏕᏣᎧᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: so'ile kehsv lha yutaluhl tiketsalihs tetsakhahv
phrases.phonetic_broad: soile kesv la yutalul tiketsalis tetsakav

phrases.phonetic_text: tskwhihsti'e
phrases.phonetic_broad: tskwistie
phrases.english_text: Yes, a lot of them!

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎯᎠᏛ ᎢᏧᎳᎮᏃ Ꮲ ᏱᏓᏂᎶᏐᏂ ᏍᎩᏅ ᏗᎨᏣᎵᏏ ᏳᎾᏚᎵ ᏢᏴ ᎤᎾᏛᎪᏗ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: hi'atv itsulahen tlv yitanilohson skin tiketsalihs yuntuli lvyv unthvkoti hiwonihskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: iatv itsulaen tlv yitaniloson skin tiketsalis yuntuli lvyv untvkoti iwoniskv
phrases.english_text: Both of us, someday we’ll pass on. Then your grandkids might want to hear you talking.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏅ ᏳᎾᏓᏙᎮᎳ ᏳᏂᎷᏣ ᏱᎨᎦᎵᏍᎪᎸᏓᏏ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏧᎾᏛᎪᏗ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬᎢ
phrases.phonetic_text: skinv yuntatohel yuniluhts yikekalihskoltahs kehehst tsunahthvkot hiwnhsk'i
phrases.phonetic_broad: skinv yuntatoel yuniluts yikekaliskoltas keest tsunatvkot iwnski
phrases.english_text: If they ask and come here, they will let them listen to it.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏯᎾᏛᏓᏍᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: yanthvtahsta
phrases.phonetic_broad: yantvtasta
phrases.english_text: There they can listen to it.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv vv
phrases.english_text: Yes, yes.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᎬᏱ ᎨᎲ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎧᎵ ᏕᏣᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏌ
phrases.phonetic_text: akvyi kehv yonek khali tetsato'v skhinohihsa
phrases.phonetic_broad: akvyi kev yonek kali tetsatov skinoisa
phrases.english_text: First thing, tell me your full English name.

phrases.phonetic_text: tsalakna
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsalakna
phrases.english_text: And in Cherokee?

phrases.phonetic_text: mel makayi
phrases.phonetic_broad: mel makayi
phrases.english_text: Me-li Ma-Ga-Yi.

phrases.phonetic_text: makayi
phrases.phonetic_broad: makayi
phrases.english_text: Ma-Ga-Yi…

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᏣᎵ Shell ᏓᏩᏙᎠ
phrases.phonetic_text: ayt tshal hsaw tawato'a
phrases.phonetic_broad: ayt tsal saw tawatoa
phrases.english_text: For me, Charlie Shell is my name.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᎳᎩᏃ ᎬᏗ ᏩᎴᎵ ᏓᏩᏙᎠ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsalakin kvti wale'li twto'a
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsalakin kvti waleli twtoa
phrases.english_text: In Cherokee it is Wa-Le-Li (Hummingbird)

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏩᎴᎵ ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: wlli v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: wlli vv
phrases.english_text: Wa-Le-Li.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᏢ ᏣᏕᏁ
phrases.phonetic_text: hatl tsatenhe
phrases.phonetic_broad: atl tsatene
phrases.english_text: Where were you born?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏩᏕᏅᎩ ᏗᏓᏁᎸᏭᎮᏃ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᎡᎵ ᏍᏓᏱ
phrases.phonetic_text: awatenhvhki titanelvwhenho awatenhv elhi stayi
phrases.phonetic_broad: awatenvki titanelvweno awatenv eli stayi
phrases.english_text: I was born at home. It was pretty hard.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᎦᏓᏅᏒᎮᏃ ᎥᎿ ᏗᏩᏕᏅ ᎾᎮᏃ Caney ᎢᎯᏲ ᎤᏪᏴ ᎾᎥ ᏣᏃᏎᎲ ᏪᎵᏂ ᏗᏜ ᏚᏭᎪᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: okata'nvhsvhenho vnh tiwtenhv nahen kheni ihiyo uweyv na'v tsanohsehv welin titl tuwukohtv
phrases.phonetic_broad: okatanvsveno vn tiwtenv naen keni iiyo uweyv nav tsanosev welin titl tuwukotv
phrases.english_text: We have moved from where I was born there at Caney, near Caney Creek, they called it, towards Welling.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Yes.

phrases.phonetic_text: v'v

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᏢ ᎨᎲ Ꮩ ᏣᏛᏏᏙᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: hatlhv kehv to tsathvhsitolv
phrases.phonetic_broad: atlv kev to tsatvsitolv
phrases.english_text: Where for sure you grew up at, there? Where you’re talking about?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎿᎨ ᏥᏃᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: vnhak tshinohe
phrases.phonetic_broad: vnak tsinoe
phrases.english_text: Where for sure you grew up at, there? Where you’re talking about?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎯᏍᎩ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᎥᎿ ᏬᎦᏓᏅᏌᏃ ᏃᏭ ᎦᏚᏏ Babo ᎠᏃᏎᎲ ᏃᏭᏃ ᏩᏩᏛᏒ

phrases.phonetic_broad: isk tsutetiyvta awatenv vna wokatanvsn now katus tato anosev nowno wawatsv
phrases.english_text: Five years I lived there. We moved then to the top of the mountain, “Ba-Bo” they called it, where I grew up at.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᏍ Sam MccoyᎢᏍ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏨᏂ ᎨᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: nahs hsam makho'ihs kohuhst tsvnhi kehe
phrases.phonetic_broad: nas sam makois koust tsvni kee

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᎶᏏᏅ ᎦᏳᎳᏅ ᏍᏈᏍᏗ ᏚᎾᏛᎦᎾ Ꮭ ᏱᎩᎾᏝᏃᎮᏞ Guy ᎠᏎ ᏍᏓᏝᏃᎮᏞ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsalohsnv kaylnv skwihst tunthvkana tla yikintlanohelhe ka ahs stalhanohele
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsalosnv kaylnv skwist tuntvkana tla yikintlanoele ka as stalanoele
phrases.english_text: Brother-in-law… You’ve been through this before already, a lot of them have heard it. It wasn’t me that you talked to, it was probably Guy.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏏᏭᏅ ᏛᎦᏁᎸᏔᏂ ᏍᏗ ᎩᏂᏃᎮᏗ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏗᏣᎶᏒ ᎨᏒ ᏂᎯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ ᎥᎾ
phrases.phonetic_text: siwn tvkanelhvhthani sti kininohehti nuhst titsalohsv kehsv nihi skina skhinohihsi vna
phrases.phonetic_broad: siwn tvkanelvtani sti kininoeti nust titsalosv kesv nii skina skinoisi vna
phrases.english_text: But I will try again. We have to talk a little about where you came from. Tell me about when you were a kid, what was it like where you all came from, what you all played, or everything you all did. Tell me about that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎯ ᎯᏲᏟ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏗᏥᎶᏒ ᏕᏣᏁᎶᏂᏙᎸ ᏂᎦᏓᎴ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏂᏣᏛᏁᎯ ᏍᎩᎾᎭ ᏥᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ
phrases.phonetic_text: nihi hiyoli tsikehv nuhstv titsilohsv tetsanelonhitol nikatal kohuhsti nitsatvnehi skinaha tsihskinohihsi
phrases.phonetic_broad: nii iyoli tsikev nustv titsilosv tetsanelonitol nikatal kousti nitsatvnei skinaa tsiskinoisi
phrases.english_text: But I will try again. We have to talk a little about where you came from. Tell me about when you were a kid, what was it like where you all came from, what you all played, or everything you all did. Tell me about that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎿᎮᏃ babo ᎠᎩᎷᏨᎢ Eight
phrases.phonetic_text: vnhhen tato aki'luhtsv'i et
phrases.phonetic_broad: vnen tato akilutsvi et
phrases.english_text: I came to Barber when I was 18 months old. Mom and Dad had divorced. We came to Barber, and Dad was living in Vian. My brother is older than me. He also grew up in Vian. I grew up in Barber. When us kids were playing around, there was mostly Cherokee kids that lived there, when we were playing.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᏁᎳᏚ ᎢᏯᏅᏓ ᎦᎨᎥ ᎠᎩᎷᏨᎢ ᎡᏥᎮᏃ ᎡᏙᏓᏃ ᏚᎾᎦᎴᏅᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: na nelatu iynvt kake'v aki'luhtsv'i etsihenho etotan tunkalenvha
phrases.phonetic_broad: na nelatu iynvt kakev akilutsvi etsieno etotan tunkalenva
phrases.english_text: I came to Barber when I was 18 months old. Mom and Dad had divorced. We came to Barber, and Dad was living in Vian. My brother is older than me. He also grew up in Vian. I grew up in Barber. When us kids were playing around, there was mostly Cherokee kids that lived there, when we were playing.

phrases.english_text: I came to Barber when I was 18 months old. Mom and Dad had divorced. We came to Barber, and Dad was living in Vian. My brother is older than me. He also grew up in Vian. I grew up in Barber. When us kids were playing around, there was mostly Cherokee kids that lived there, when we were playing.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏃᏭᏅ ᎥᎿᏭ ᏃᏭ Babo ᏗᏜ ᏩᏩᏛᏏᏙᎸ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏙᏣᏁᎶᏂᏙᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎤᏟ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏁᎲ ᎥᎿ ᏙᏣᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬᎢ
phrases.phonetic_text: nowunhv vnhawu nw tato titl wawathvhsitolv nownhv totsanelonhitohv tiniyolhi tskwihsti anitsalak tiniyolhi utli ika anehv vnha totsanelohvhskv'i
phrases.phonetic_broad: nowunv vnawu nw tato titl wawatvsitolv nownv totsanelonitov tiniyoli tskwisti anitsalak tiniyoli utli ika anev vna totsanelovskvi
phrases.english_text: I came to Barber when I was 18 months old. Mom and Dad had divorced. We came to Barber, and Dad was living in Vian. My brother is older than me. He also grew up in Vian. I grew up in Barber. When us kids were playing around, there was mostly Cherokee kids that lived there, when we were playing.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᎳ ᏂᏥᎡ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: hala nitsi'e sitanelv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ala nitsie sitanelv

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏦᎢᏛ ᏃᏥ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎠᏱᏃ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸᎢᏃ ᏐᎢ
phrases.phonetic_text: tso'itv notsi vkito ayin tsohstatalv'ihn s'i
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsoitv notsi vkito ayin tsostatalvin si
phrases.english_text: There are three of us, my brother, me, and my sister.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎦᏓᎲ Ꮟ ᎢᏤᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: nikathv si itseha
phrases.phonetic_broad: nikatv si itsea
phrases.english_text: Are all of you still living?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏤᎭ ᏦᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨᏃ Ᏺ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎤᎾᏂᎩᏌ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v nkata otseha tsokikayvlkenho y kayla unanhikhsa
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv nkata otsea tsokikayvlkeno y kayla unaniksa
phrases.english_text: Yes, all of us are still alive. Our parents are already gone.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᎳ ᎢᎩᏓ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎢᏤᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: hala ikhit khalihtsote itsehe
phrases.phonetic_broad: ala ikit kalitsote itsee
phrases.english_text: How big was the house you all lived in?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏤᎲ ᎥᎿ Ꮎ ᎢᎯᏲ ᏄᏪᏴ ᎾᎥ ᏦᏤᎲ ᏔᎵ
phrases.phonetic_text: otsehv vnha na ihiy nwey na'v tsotsehv thal
phrases.phonetic_broad: otsev vna na iiy nwey nav tsotsev tal
phrases.english_text: We lived near where Caney Creek was. We lived in a four-bedroom house there. There were fireplaces on both sides. When we were chased off, they took and moved half of the house. Then they brought it to the hill in Barber. And then, when they built onto the end of it, it became six bedrooms.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏅᎩᏛ ᏕᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᎣᏤᎲ ᎥᎿ ᏗᎪᏘᏗ

phrases.phonetic_broad: nvkitv tkanvsulv otsev vna tikotti
phrases.english_text: We lived near where Caney Creek was. We lived in a four-bedroom house there. There were fireplaces on both sides. When we were chased off, they took and moved half of the house. Then they brought it to the hill in Barber. And then, when they built onto the end of it, it became six bedrooms.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏗᎪᏢᎯ ᎢᏧᎳ ᏗᎬᎩᏗ ᎥᏍᎩᏃ ᎣᎩᎨᎯᏙᎳ ᏃᏭ ᎠᏰᏟᏭ ᎢᎦ ᎤᏂᏫᏛᎲ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎤᏂᎲᏒ ᏃᏭ Babo ᎦᏚᏏ ᏭᏂᏲᏢ
phrases.phonetic_text: tikotlhvhi itshul tikvkhiti vhskino okikhehitol nowu ayelhiwu ika uniwhitvhv kalihtsote unihvhsv nwu tato ka'tuhs wniyholhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tikotlvi itsul tikvkiti vskino okikeitol nowu ayeliwu ika uniwitvv kalitsote univsv nwu tato katus wniyolv
phrases.english_text: We lived near where Caney Creek was. We lived in a four-bedroom house there. There were fireplaces on both sides. When we were chased off, they took and moved half of the house. Then they brought it to the hill in Barber. And then, when they built onto the end of it, it became six bedrooms.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎿ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏚᎾᏁᏍᎨᎲ ᎠᏍᏛ ᏗᏜ ᏚᏂᏁᏉᎥ ᏃᏭ ᏑᏓᎵ ᏗᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᏃᏭ

phrases.english_text: We lived near where Caney Creek was. We lived in a four-bedroom house there. There were fireplaces on both sides. When we were chased off, they took and moved half of the house. Then they brought it to the hill in Barber. And then, when they built onto the end of it, it became six bedrooms.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏔᎾᎲ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: uthanhv klitste
phrases.phonetic_broad: utanv klitste
phrases.english_text: It was a big house, huh?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎦᎸᎳᏗᏃ ᎪᏢᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: khalvla'tin kolhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: kalvlatin kolv
phrases.english_text: It was tall too.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᎤᏰᏟᏕ ᎣᎩᎨᎯᏙᎳ ᏣᏗᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: to uyelhihte okikhehitola tstha
phrases.phonetic_broad: to uyelite okikeitola tsta

phrases.phonetic_broad: o nano amayi
phrases.english_text: Oh, the creek!

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ ᏗᏂᏍᏚᏂᏎᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: o tinihstunhsete
phrases.phonetic_broad: o tinistunsete

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏩᎦᏲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏁ ᏙᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: wakayo ohst nuntvn thv
phrases.phonetic_broad: wakayo ost nuntvn tv
phrases.english_text: The cows had it good though?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏅ ᏌᏌ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏚᏂᎾᏝᎥ ᎾᏅ ᏗᏈᏍᏙ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᎡᏥ Ꮎ ᎤᏄᏱᏔᏅ ᎦᏤᏍᏙ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏙᎩᎾᎥ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: ohst nuntn sahsa skw tstuninalha'v nanhv tikwhst tstekolhskv etshi na unuythanv katsehsto skwu tsitokina'v skiyuhsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: ost nuntn sasa skw tstuninalav nanv tikwst tstekolskv etsi na unuytanv katsesto skwu tsitokinav skiyusti
phrases.english_text: They had it good. We also had geese. Mama would make pillows with the feathers, and mattresses too.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᎮᏃ ᎦᏌᎴᎾ ᏏᏛᎮ ᏴᏩᏔ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ Ꮎ goose down ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎪᏢᏔᏅ ᏧᎦᎾᏫ ᎥᏍᎩ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: skihen kahsalena sitvhe ywhath khitsik na kuhs tan shki yhst tikolhvhthanv tsukanwi vhski iyhsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: skien kasalena sitve ywat kitsik na kus tan ski yst tikolvtanv tsukanwi vski iysti
phrases.english_text: Jackets today, you can still find them made with goose down. Those that are made like that are really warm.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎮᎨ ᏗᎬᏄ
phrases.phonetic_text: itsalhsteliheke tikvnu
phrases.phonetic_broad: itsalstelieke tikvnu
phrases.english_text: Did you all help with… how do you say…

phrases.phonetic_text: tokhe yta
phrases.phonetic_broad: toke yta
phrases.english_text: Did you all help with… how do you say…

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏗᎬᏄᏯᎩᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: tikvnykita
phrases.phonetic_broad: tikvnykita
phrases.english_text: Plucking their feathers.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᏦᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᎡᎵᏏᎮᏃ ᏗᎯᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᏭᏃ Ꭰ ᏥᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᏥᏓᏍᏆᏄᏖᏲ ᏥᏓᎯᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v tsho'tslhstelihv elihsihen tihihi tskehv nhawno a tshintekvnehv tsitahskwanutheyo tsthihv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv tsotslsteliv elisien tiii tskev nawno a tsintekvnev tsitaskwanuteyo tstiv
phrases.english_text: We helped. Grandma used to kill them and then she went like this [gestures] when she twisted their necks when she killed them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᏔᎦᏛ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏗᎮ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsithaktv utloy tihe tskhv thv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsitaktv utloy tie tskv tv
phrases.english_text: Kill chickens the same way back then, ain’t it? Did you all have a good garden back then?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏲᎨ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏓᏥᏫᏒᏗ ᏄᏍᏕ ᏍᎩ ᏲᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: yokhe ohst tatsiwhihsvt nuhste ski yonhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: yoke ost tatsiwisvt nuste ski yonv
phrases.english_text: Kill chickens the same way back then, ain’t it? Did you all have a good garden back then?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎥᎿᏅ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏃᏭ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏍᏊ ᏧᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᎡᎵ ᎣᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎣᎬᏌ ᎣᎩᏍᏚᏟᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᎠᎹ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v vnhanhv elat nhow ka'tuhs skwu tsuwokiluhtshv eli ohsi tsikehv ahseno okvhsa okihstutlihst tskehv nowu ama
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv vnanv elat now katus skwu tsuwokilutsv eli osi tsikev aseno okvsa okistutlist tskev nowu ama
phrases.english_text: Yes, below. When we got to the mountain it was good, but we had to water it ourselves.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: totv
phrases.phonetic_broad: totv
phrases.english_text: You did?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎲ ᎥᎿ ᎨᏓᎵ ᎨᎲ Ᏺ Ꮎ ᏓᏓᏑᎶᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎯᏌᏛᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: vhv vnha khetli kehv yo na tatahsulohskv ohst tsinikalhstihv na amayulhiht kehv ahihsathskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv vna ketli kev yo na tatasuloskv ost tsinikalstiv na amayulit kev aisatskv
phrases.english_text: Uh-huh, down the hill it would give off dew. By the creek it did really good with the morning dew.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᎢᏨᏁᎮ ᎢᏥᏓᎷᎩᏍᎨ
phrases.phonetic_text: to itsvnhe ithsitalukihske
phrases.phonetic_broad: to itsvne itsitalukiske
phrases.english_text: How did y’all plow the ground?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏐᏈᎵ ᏥᏓᏅᏗᎲ ᎦᏓᎷᎪᏗ ᏗᏂᎴᏅᎯᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: sokwl tstanhvhtihv katlukot tinilenvhita
phrases.phonetic_broad: sokwl tstanvtiv katlukot tinilenvita
phrases.english_text: They used a horse-drawn plow, and donkeys.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏕᏥᎾᏝᎡᎨ ᎩᎶᎨ ᏄᏓᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: ttsinalha'ek khilok nutale
phrases.phonetic_broad: ttsinalaek kilok nutale
phrases.english_text: Did you own them or did someone else?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏙ ᏥᏚᎾᏝᎥ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎥ ᏥᏂᏚᎾᏓᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: elihs tsikhv uto tsitunalha'v vhskin na'v tsintuntalv
phrases.phonetic_broad: elis tsikv uto tsitunalav vskin nav tsintuntalv
phrases.english_text: Grandma’s brother owned them. They were neighbors.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏣᏛᏁ
phrases.phonetic_text: t skwu ohst nitsatvnhe
phrases.phonetic_broad: t skwu ost nitsatvne
phrases.english_text: Y’all had it really good there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏃᎦᏛᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: ika ohst nokatnhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ika ost nokatnv
phrases.english_text: We did really well.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏴᏣᏚᎳᎨ ᏫᎦᏤᏓᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᏣᏛᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: ytsatulkhe wkatsthsti yki sk tsnuhst tsathsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ytsatulke wkatststi yki sk tsnust tsatsv
phrases.english_text: Would you want to go back there, to the way it was when you grew up?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᎥᎲ ᎬᏇᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᎹᏰ ᏱᎩ ᎠᎮ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏳᏫᎨᏓ Ꮎ ᏥᏳ ᎩᎶ ᎬᏆᏘᏃᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎥᎿᎮᏃ Ᏼ ᏭᎵᏍᏙ ᏴᏓᎭ ᎠᎹᏱ ᏭᏏᏅᏌ
phrases.phonetic_text: awatulhv vhv kkwetahsti amay yki ahe eliwu yuwket nha tsiyu khilo kvkwthinhohihsti yiki vnhahen y wulhsto ytaha amayi wuhsinvhsa

phrases.english_text: Uh-huh, I do want to go back there. I could go to the water if someone would bring me in a boat, because sometimes the water edge would be right there when the water receded.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎯᎢᏛ ᏱᏣᏛᏁᏗ ᏦᎮᎮᎢᏍ ᏣᏥ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsatelhohkwa'v tsatahstayvhti hi'itv yitsatvnt tsohehe'ihs tsatsi
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsatelokwav tsatastayvti iitv yitsatvnt tsoeeis tsatsi
phrases.english_text: When you learned to cook, did your mom tell you, “This is how to cook”? Or did you just watch her?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᎪᎨ ᎯᎦᏙᏍᏛᏭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsikokhe hikathohstvwu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsikoke ikatostvwu
phrases.english_text: When you learned to cook, did your mom tell you, “This is how to cook”? Or did you just watch her?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᎦᏙᏍᏛᏊ ᏥᏛᏆᎴᏅᎲ ᏃᏭᏃ ᏢᏴ ᏃᏭ ᏣᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗᏛ ᏃᏭ ᎥᏉᎮᎲ ᏣᏆᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏃᏭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsikathohstvkw tsitvkwlenvhv nown tlhv'y nohw tsatehlkwahsttv nowu vkwohehv tsakwatelhohkwa'v nowu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsikatostvkw tsitvkwlenvv nown tlvy now tsatelkwasttv nowu vkwoev tsakwatelokwav nowu
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᎴᏍᏊ ᏣᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᎤᏅᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: elihs tskehv nowlehskwu tsawyhohvhskv na anikayvli unvnhihstoht kohuhst
phrases.phonetic_broad: elis tskev nowleskwu tsawyovskv na anikayvli unvnistot koust
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏗ ᏓᏃᏎᎰ ᏗᎫᎮ ᏥᏕᎪᎮᎲ Ꮎ Corn Bread ᎯᎢᏴ ᎢᏗᎩᏓ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: toti tanohseho tikhe tsitekohehv na khawn twat hi'iyv itikhit tstekolhskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: toti tanoseo tike tsitekoev na kawn twat iiyv itikit tstekolskv
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.phonetic_text: anihsowlvhs
phrases.phonetic_broad: anisowlvs
phrases.english_text: Are they round?

phrases.phonetic_text: anihsowal tak hathshe tanohsehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: anisowal tak atse tanosev
phrases.english_text: The round ones they called dog heads.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v akilkwtv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv akilkwtv
phrases.english_text: Yes, I really liked them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᎾᏅ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᏉᏢᏗ ᏣᏇᏲᏅ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏚᏯ ᎠᏑᏱ ᎦᏚ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏪᏲᏅ ᎤᏖᏗ

phrases.phonetic_broad: skinanv iyust tikwolvti tsakweyon nowl tuya asuy katu nowl tsaweynv uteti

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᏛ ᏥᏕᎯᏃᎮ dog heads ᎤᏗᏞᎩ ᎪᎢ ᎠᎻᏃ ᎠᏑᏴ
phrases.phonetic_text: nat tsithinohe tak haths utilhek ko'i amino ahsuyv
phrases.phonetic_broad: nat tsitinoe tak ats utilek koi amino asuyv

phrases.phonetic_text: toyu utht tekhan kwihs ahsuynhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: toyu utt tekan kwis asuynv
phrases.english_text: It’s really delicious, with bacon grease mixed in.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏧᏍᏆᎸᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsuhskwlvte
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsuskwlvte
phrases.english_text: Sure is that way.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᏍᎩᏃ ᏍᏊ ᎣᎬᏌᎮᏃ ᏦᏦᏢᏍᎬ Ꮎ butter ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏖᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎦᏅᎵᏰᏗ Ꮎ dog heads
phrases.phonetic_text: vhskin skwu okvhshen tsotsolhvhskv na tata tohy skwu utheht skin tkanvliyet n tak haths
phrases.phonetic_broad: vskin skwu okvsen tsotsolvskv na tata toy skwu utet skin tkanvliyet n tak ats
phrases.english_text: We also made our own butter. It was also really delicious to spread on them, the dog heads.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ Ꮭ Ᏺ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᏁᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: o l yo ilhiy ski ykvnlv
phrases.phonetic_broad: o l yo iliy ski ykvnlv
phrases.english_text: I’ve never tried it that way.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎪᏢᏅ butter ᎤᏅᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ
phrases.phonetic_text: tyu utheht ski skwu uwahs kolhvnhv tata unvtinhv skwu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tyu utet ski skwu uwas kolvnv tata unvtinv skwu

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᎾ ᎤᎦᏗᏢᏓ creamᎢᏍ ᏣᏃᏢᏍᎪ
phrases.phonetic_text: nana uktilhvt khwimihs tsanolhvhsko
phrases.phonetic_broad: nana uktilvt kwimis tsanolvsko
phrases.english_text: What about what they call cream? Did you all milk the cows?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᏊᏅ ᏕᏥᏁᎩᎡᎮ ᏩᎦ
phrases.phonetic_text: shkwunv tetsineki'ehe wka
phrases.phonetic_broad: skwunv tetsinekiee wka
phrases.english_text: What about what they call cream? Did you all milk the cows?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭵ ᏙᏥᏁᎩᎡᎲ ᏍᎩᏅ cream ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦᎾᏕᎬᎮᏅ cream butterᎢᏃ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦᎾᏕᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: v ttsineki'ehv skinhv khwim skw tsikantekvhenhv khwim tata'ino skwu tsikantekv
phrases.phonetic_broad: v ttsinekiev skinv kwim skw tsikantekvenv kwim tataino skwu tsikantekv
phrases.english_text: Yes, we milked them. That cream too, she sold the cream and also butter.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᏗᎨᏣᏙ ᏗᏣᏓᎸᎴ ᏱᎩ ᏂᎦᏗᏍ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎢᏥᏬᏂᏍᎨ
phrases.phonetic_text: n tiketsato titsatalvle yik nikatihs tsalaki itswonhihske
phrases.phonetic_broad: n tiketsato titsatalvle yik nikatis tsalaki itswoniske
phrases.english_text: Your brothers or sisters, did you all speak Cherokee?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎦᏬᏂ ᎾᏍᏊ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏥᏬᏂ ᏣᎳᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: na vkito kawoni nahskw tsohsttalv nhikata otsiwhoni tsalahkhi
phrases.phonetic_broad: na vkito kawoni naskw tsosttalv nikata otsiwoni tsalaki
phrases.english_text: My brother speaks and so does my sister. We all speak Cherokee.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏏᏍ ᏕᏣᏓᏩᏛᎯᏙᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: sihs tetstawhahthvhitoho
phrases.phonetic_broad: sis tetstawatvitoo
phrases.english_text: Do you all still visit one another?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎲᎥ ᏞᏍᏗ ᏗᎦᏥᎪᎥ ᏔᎵᏚ ᎢᏯᏆᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎩᎳ ᎦᏥᎪᎥ ᎠᏯ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏲᎵᎩ ᏱᎩ ᎰᏩ ᎥᎿ ᏗᏜ
phrases.phonetic_text: hv'v tlhsti tkathsik'v tha'ltu iykwatethiyt khi'l katsiko'v ay'a vkito etota hehst skwu tsiyoliki yk howa vnha ttla

phrases.english_text: Uh-uh, I didn’t ever see them. I was twelve years old before I ever saw them, my dad and brother. I don’t really know him that way.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ ᏝᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: o tlthe
phrases.phonetic_broad: o tlte
phrases.english_text: Oh, not really?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎲᎥ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎰᏩ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᎩ ᏱᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: hv'v hehst how khatsiyolikhi yiki
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv est ow katsiyoliki yiki
phrases.english_text: No, I don’t really know them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎾ ᏕᏣᏓᏘᎿᎥ ᏣᎳᎩᏍ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: nina tetsatathinha'v tsalkihs aniwonihski

phrases.english_text: Yes, I only knew my grandmother, my mom’s mom, and her grandma had come on the Trail of Tears. She came when she was a little girl. What she was told, Grandma told me about it. This last time we went back, I could only see shadows of the mountains. It was really bad for them, the way the Indians were treated, she told me when she [Great Grandma] was a little girl coming on that trail.

phrases.english_text: The soldiers took everything from them. Somewhere they were locked up, they say, gathering them all together for that forced march. A lot of them died while they were rounded up.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏝᎮᏃ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᎬᎾᏈᏴᎰ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏲ ᏂᏚᏅᏁᎴ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᎠᏯᎮᏃ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᏍᏊ ᏁᎳᎩ ᏂᎩᎦᏛᎴᏒᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᎮᏃ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᎭ ᏫᏥᏯᏘᏂᏓᏍᏗ

phrases.english_text: My wife, I’m thinking about taking her there to Georgia. Vann Mansion, they talk about, Vann was my wife’s last name. Jim Vann owned Vann Mansion. Somewhere there they were left behind they say, her relatives. I don’t know for sure; I just want to take her there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏃ Marble City ᏣᏛᎦᏅ Ꮎ Marble City

phrases.english_text: For me, Marble City, you’ve heard of Marble City? If somebody died over there, that’s your family, they’d say. I didn’t know anything about that.

phrases.english_text: That’s what I told my boys growing up in Dry Creek. “Don’t look for girls over there, you’re related to everybody”. They really believed it; they didn’t do that.

phrases.english_text: They are trying. I go to Tulsa, and I go here in town. When it gets worse, I go to Tulsa, when they can’t help me here. It started as glaucoma. They didn’t know what it was here at first, when it started. Something happened inside and they couldn’t fix it. One time we went to Crosslin, a healer that lived in Sallisaw. And he took me to water. Really a wonder what happened then, the way my eyes are now, I can’t see anything. It’s just white is all I see in here. I can’t see you two. phrases.english_text: That’s how it was sometimes when people were around, they would tell stories. What happened in the past, and then at night she started telling me things until I was asleep. How Grandma described it to me was a little different, but there was one thing she used to talk about. There was a tree, and the women, there were these beans that grew back then, they would go up the mountain looking for where those beans grew, to cook them. About halfway up, they were sitting down when something started making a sound. When they looked up there, there was something standing between the tree branches. The girl said there was something tall in between the branches, it looked like a star she said, Grandma said. When we were there in the valley where they had been, I didn’t go. It was too rough for me to go, I was told. They were saying there were markings, something that Juhlgal had done. They said those markings, no one can read what it’s saying. They said when they went, some of them went to look at it. They say that Juhlgal had done that, they were saying.

phrases.english_text: Yes, she told me a lot of things. And the Indians that were there, they danced, and one time they were saying if a panther was coming it would howl. If a panther was coming, they would stay behind to build fires at the dance ground, because the panther was afraid of fire. One time they left behind a blind old woman, she was staying at their home. She could hear the panther growling as it was coming near. The old woman didn’t know what she was going to do. “When it finds out I am in here, it will come eat me,” the old woman thought. So, she heated up some water, bringing it to a boil. Sure enough, the panther came in. The houses that they lived in were like tents covered in tree leaves, and when it opened the woman sat there, and did this [gestures] to the panther. When it opened, the panther was splashed with hot water, and it ran off, backing away because it had been scalded. The next morning, the dancers returned, and the panther wasn’t there. It was hurt too badly, and so the dancers had to go kill it.

phrases.english_text: They were bad. One time she said, “This man’s wife was running around on him. So, she went to a dance and left the boy to stay with his grandma.” I think they were staying with her. “Let her go,” Grandma told the boy when the wife left. She didn’t take much of her things. The old woman sat in front of the fireplace and put all she had down. And there, the boy saw she had laid out some arrowheads. She had hung what they call a moccasin––you know the kind made out of deer skin––she hung it in front of where she had the arrowheads. Later on, she left and one of the arrowheads made a sound, so she went to where the bundle was on the chimney. Later on, when she came back, she said to the flint, “You didn’t do anything.” So then she sent another arrowhead and again when it came back it hadn’t done anything. “You didn’t go do anything either,” she said to it. Then she put it away. When the third one left and came back she had a container this [gestures] size with water, and the arrowhead went into it. It was washed, and the arrowhead had blood on it. “You really did something,” she said to it, then she put it up. Later on, someone came and told the boy that his wife had died at the dance. The flint must have shot her.

phrases.english_text: Another one? Let's see… because there’s a lot of things I know. Also, the Ukten that they talk about, have you all heard of it? One time she said they went fishing. Standing Rock, as they call it, by Oklahoma Station, near where the river is. Standing Rock, as they called it, because Grandma said a rock used to stand there. It’s underwater. These days the water isn’t as deep as she was saying around that area. There, a tree that had fallen was there. Grandma would sit on it before others started coming to fish there in the deep end. Long dresses, they wore back then. Her dress was in the way of her fishing. After a while something was moving below, she saw it and looked. It looked like a cow. It was looking at her from below. It was kind of like a greenish color, she said. Its eyes were like a cow, and its nose too, and it had horns. She watched it, she thought, “What am I going to do?” The others fishing there, she didn’t want to yell at them. “Let’s get down for a little while,” she told them, walking away. “Let’s get down for a while”. They all started walking back. They didn’t ask why when they were told to get off. When they went up a little further, she told them, and that’s when they started running, she said. That was Ukten, she used to say. That’s where it lives, she used to say, in the deep end of the water, there near Standing Rock. I think there are still some things that are living in the deep end of the water.

phrases.english_text: One time we took the kids there, it really was dangerous because I didn't know how to swim. We took them, and Sam, that you said, he’s not living now, he was killed by a car. It was hard for him to mind; he was going towards the deep. “Come back, come back,” I was saying. Over here were the other kids. He was still going and the younger boy got out, and we were calling him to come back. He’d just giggle. After a while something came up behind him, and he was facing us. It came up so far, it was like a snake and was this [gestures] big. Pretty big. It had eyes when it came up. That’s when I started hollering “Come here, come here!” I was telling him. That girl too, she started jumping around. “Come back!” Then the boy started to run back. All of a sudden, it came up, that thing like a snake. Not too long after, my husband was working at Six Shooter, somebody came there in a boat. He said someone there saw a big snake-like thing floating in the water, they said, below that rock bluff. I didn’t know what it was, but it was pretty long. Something like a snake it was, that the others had seen.

phrases.english_text: Yes, those too. She told one about when they were taking care of a sick person, the medicine man was doctoring them and couldn’t cure them. Then someone checked. A raven is disturbing this one. They can’t get better unless it takes them, she was told. Unless you get somebody brave and young. You get them, tonight this doorway on both sides they will sit, because the raven will come back, they were told. There were two brave young men. “We will do it!” they said. They used medicine on them and were seated next to the doorway. Back then when somebody was sick, people would come, they would be outside and have a fire going, that’s how they were. The young men that were treated with medicine heard something in the distance. They had been told what was going to happen. They were waiting on it. The second time they heard the noise it was a little closer, and a third, and a fourth, and then on the steps landed a beautiful woman. She wore a long knife on her side, as she walked, she didn’t see the boys watching over the sick person. When the woman got to the doorway, the boys grabbed her. She was very strong, I think. She almost got away from the young boys. She was slinging them around, but they held on to her until morning came. That morning, when it got light out, they let her go. The woman was naked. The dress she had was covered in corn and it broke and left her naked. I don’t know if she lived close by or not. Nobody heard anything about anyone passing away, because she was going to die when she got home, they were told. But they didn’t hear anything. I guess she must’ve lived too far away. Then the sick person began to get better. That’s what was coming to the sickly person, that raven demon.
